items.title: Meet the 2026 App Store Award finalists
items.summary: Apple announced the finalists for the 2026 App Store Awards, recognizing 45 developers from around the world for exceptional apps and games.
items.body:
Today, Apple announced 45 finalists for this year’s App Store Awards, celebrating developers from around the world whose apps and games exemplify the very best in technical innovation, user experience, and design. This year’s finalists span iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Vision Pro, Apple Watch, Apple TV, and Apple Arcade, as well as the Cultural Impact category. Winners will be announced in the coming weeks.

“We’re excited to celebrate this year’s App Store Award finalists, whose creativity has brought extraordinary apps and games to life for users around the world,” said Carson Oliver, Apple’s vice president of App Store. “From games that transport players to imaginative new worlds and bring out the fun of playing together, to apps that empower users to learn new skills and make a difference in their communities, these developers are redefining how we connect, create, and experience the world.”

ElevenReader, for reading aloud text in surprisingly natural-sounding AI voices.

(Not Boring) Camera, for transforming iPhone into a customizable old-school camera.

Raylie, for offering a personalized, guided journey for every flight.

BALL x PIT, for breaking the mold of brick breakers.

DAVE THE DIVER, for exploring the oceans deep.

Gambonanza, for rewiring the rules of chess.

Cosmos, for inspiring users with a gorgeous mood board.

Kiddopia, for giving little ones a joyful space to learn and play.

Mockup, for helping everyone design the website or app of their dreams.

Aniimo, for forging fantasy quests with truly adorable creatures.

Arknights: Endfield, for waging stunning battles on a faraway moon.

Where Winds Meet, for creating cinematic martial arts moves.

Paste, for supercharging the Mac Clipboard.

Things 3, for tackling tasks with simplicity.

Ulysses, for making it easy to create beautifully styled documents.

Big Walk, for encouraging friends to puzzle together.

Blue Prince, for delivering a mysterious mansion full of unexpected twists.

Crimson Desert, for creating a sprawling war-torn fantasyland.

Perchang World, for stumping players with marble-filled physics puzzles.

PowerWash Simulator, for making fighting grime so satisfying.

Pusheen’s Place, for captivating users with really cute cats.

Adobe Premiere, for letting creators edit video on an expansive spatial canvas.

MLB, for livestreaming baseball games from behind home plate.

Museas, for turning the living room into a gorgeous art gallery.

Cueva de las Manos, for designing one-of-a-kind puzzles that play with light and shadow.

Ping Pong Club, for bringing smashing rounds of table tennis.

Spatial Ops, for immersing players in first-person battles that go down right in their home.

Bevel, for turning fitness data into actionable insights.

Moonlitt, for highlighting upcoming lunar events.

StressWatch, for reporting real-time stress levels.

Case Solved: The London Files, for weaving fun logic puzzles into a noir murder mystery.

Letterboxd, for putting movie recommendations from critics and friends in one place.

Pocket Casts, for bringing podcasts to the big screen.

Brilliant, for teaching the foundations of math and science.

chilli, for making it easy to take political action for the planet.

Hearing Buddy, for helping people who are deaf or hard of hearing follow the conversation.

Karrot, for enabling circular economies among neighbors.

setlog, for bringing more authenticity to social media.

Unedo, for making learning Spanish a playful cultural journey.

and Roger, for telling a poignant and often challenging personal story.

Consume Me, for grappling with the realities of eating disorders.

PancitoMerge, for celebrating Mexico’s culinary culture.

Sago Mini Jinja’s Garden, for giving families a way to play together.

Spilled!, for making it fun to clean up polluted waterways.

Tiny Bookshop, for bringing a cozy, inclusive community to life.

items.title: Formula 1® Las Vegas Grand Prix™ streams live on Apple TV this weekend
items.summary: Formula 1® returns to the U.S. this weekend for the FORMULA 1® HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX™ 2026, streaming live on Apple TV.
items.body:
This weekend, the Las Vegas Grand Prix streams live on Apple TV, delivering comprehensive coverage and analysis and customizable viewing features to bring fans closer to the action.

Formula 1® returns to the U.S. this weekend for the FORMULA 1® HEINEKEN LAS VEGAS GRAND PRIX™ 2026 — streaming for free in the U.S. on Apple TV, with every session live and on demand.1

The lights shine bright on the Las Vegas Strip for the only night race in the United States. Mercedes’s Kimi Antonelli returns to the track for his second race since making history as F1’s youngest-ever Drivers’ Champion. With Mercedes having secured both the Drivers’ and Constructors’ championships, the team heads into the Las Vegas Grand Prix looking to continue its winning momentum, while the rest of the grid battle for crucial points and positions with just three races remaining in the season.

Apple TV is the U.S. home of F1 — delivering comprehensive coverage and analysis, powerful and customizable viewing features, and seamless integration across the Apple ecosystem to Apple TV subscribers.

Las Vegas Grand Prix coverage will feature English and Spanish commentary and access to up to 30 additional live feeds across all sessions, including Driver Tracker for a bird’s-eye view of the race, session timing and data feeds, a mixed onboard feed that automatically switches between cameras as the action unfolds, and a Podium feed that dynamically follows the drivers running in P1, P2, and P3 throughout.2

Viewers can also get closer to the action with Multiview, a feature that brings together up to four live feeds on a single screen for a more engaging race-day experience. And now Multiview is available on supported smart TVs in addition to Apple devices and streaming players — so more fans than ever can follow every angle and won’t miss a moment.

Viewers can get a more dynamic race-day experience with Multiview, a feature that brings together up to four live feeds on a single screen.

The race coverage will feature access to up to 30 additional live feeds across all sessions, including Driver Tracker for a bird’s-eye view of the race, session timing and data feeds, a mixed onboard feed that automatically switches between cameras as the action unfolds, and a Podium feed that dynamically follows the drivers running in P1, P2, and P3 throughout.

Fans can experience F1 on Apple TV in Dolby Atmos® and Dolby Vision®, bringing an even more immersive race-weekend experience to U.S. subscribers. Dolby Atmos surrounds fans with the sounds of race weekend, from team radio and commentary to roaring engines, on-track battles, and pit-lane intensity, while Dolby Vision offers rich colors and lifelike clarity. Together the two deliver exceptional sound and spectacular visuals that put fans at the heart of the action.

F1 in Dolby Vision and Dolby Atmos is available through the Apple TV app on supported Apple devices and compatible Dolby-enabled TVs, soundbars, and home theater systems.

Apple TV brings fans closer to the action with original programming, delivering fresh expert perspectives to race weekend and sharing deeper insights into the stories shaping F1 — from every curve, overtake, and podium.

Circuits in Focus — the dynamic track preview series featuring 2016 F1 world champion Nico Rosberg and content creator, record-breaking car builder, and driver Emelia Hartford — returns to Apple TV for the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix. Ahead of race weekend, Rosberg and Hartford take viewers inside one of F1’s most distinctive street circuits, breaking down the technical challenges, race strategies, and split-second decisions that could shape the fight for the podium.

Using the 2026 Season Pack for EA SPORTS™ F1® 25, the official video game of the FIA Formula One World Championship™, Rosberg and Hartford put fans in the driver’s seat as they navigate the Las Vegas Strip Circuit’s long, high-speed straights; tight corners; and heavy braking zones. Along the way, they reveal the key overtaking opportunities and strategic challenges of racing through the streets of Las Vegas, where cool nighttime temperatures and the circuit’s low-grip street surface could make all the difference on race day.

Fans can also look forward to fresh editions of The Fashion Circuit, Apple TV’s social-first digital content series celebrating the intersection of fashion, culture, and Formula 1. With the Las Vegas Grand Prix on the horizon, the series will spotlight standout paddock looks and statement-making race-weekend fashion inspired by the glamour and electric energy of racing under the Las Vegas lights.

Full Throttle is back with an action-packed episode fueled by high-octane thrills, adventure, and unexpected twists. Led by content creator and engineer Christina Roki, whose infectious energy and passion for all things automotive set the pace, the episode takes viewers on an exhilarating off-road adventure, delivering a fresh and entertaining take on the world of cars and racing.

Fans can follow the race after it wraps with The POV, a social series that features former Red Bull Racing senior technician Calum Nicholas and Roki reacting to key moments from the weekend. Whether highlighting decisive overtakes, strategy calls, or unexpected turning points, the series’ coverage blends technical expertise with a fan-first perspective.

Together, these shows make it easy for audiences to engage with F1 on and off the track.

Univision will simulcast Apple TV’s broadcast of the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, with race coverage beginning at 10 p.m. ET, featuring dedicated pre- and post-race programming to bring the excitement of F1 to Spanish-speaking audiences across the U.S.

Tubi Original The Fast Lane returns for its third and final live F1 altcast of the 2026 season, streaming free on Tubi for the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Hosted by YouTuber Michelle Khare (Challenge Accepted) and former racing champion and motorsports personality Justin Bell (Drive to Wynn), the creator-led altcast offers fans an alternative way to experience the high-stakes action of the Grand Prix on the iconic Las Vegas Strip Circuit. Featuring the main Apple TV race feed and onboard footage alongside real-time driver tracking and entertaining, culture-forward commentary, Tubi’s The Fast Lane closes out its inaugural season with a fresh, accessible viewing experience that complements the comprehensive live race coverage on Apple TV.

Apple TV is teaming up with Grindin Coffee — the premium coffee brand created by hip-hop icons Pusha T and Pharrell Williams in collaboration with legendary Italian roaster Lavazza — to bring the energy, excitement, and culture of Formula 1 to the heart of the Las Vegas Strip. From Thursday, November 19, through Saturday, November 21, fans can enjoy a special Apple TV x Grindin menu of curated specialty coffee creations, served at Eataly Las Vegas at Park MGM from early in the morning until late at night. It’s a chance to fuel up and soak in the excitement of the Las Vegas Grand Prix as drivers take to the streets under the lights.

Fans can keep up with their favorite teams and drivers all season long with the free Apple Sports app for iPhone. Designed for speed and simplicity, the app puts favorite leagues and teams front and center. F1 fans get real-time leaderboards, drivers’ and teams’ standings, and live updates for every qualifying, Sprint, and race session — all with quick access to the live race page on Apple TV.

With Live Activities,3 Apple Sports delivers real-time updates to the iPhone Lock Screen and Apple Watch so fans never miss a moment. Game Card Sharing lets fans share their excitement for any Grand Prix. Fans can also follow F1 across Apple TV, Apple Sports, and Apple News with My Sports, which syncs users’ favorites across supported apps.

In celebration of the Formula 1 Las Vegas Grand Prix, Apple Fitness+ has created a special cycling workout led by trainer Kym Perfetto, inspired by The Warm-Up playlist curated by Valtteri Bottas, a driver for the Cadillac Formula 1® Team and an avid cyclist, on Apple Music. Set to songs selected by Valtteri, the high-energy ride will bring the excitement and intensity of race weekend to a user’s workout.

Fans can gear up for the weekend with a special Apple Fitness+ cycling workout led by trainer Kym Perfetto and set to songs curated by driver and avid cyclist Valtteri Bottas.

Apple Music subscribers can get into race-weekend mode for the Las Vegas Grand Prix with an exclusive new DJ mix from globally renowned DJ and record producer Martin Garrix. Ten-time Grand Prix winner Valtteri Bottas, who joined Cadillac for the team’s inaugural Formula 1 season, will also debut his personal driver playlist, giving listeners a glimpse into his musical tastes and the songs that fuel his passion on and off the track. Subscribers can explore Apple Music’s curated collection celebrating the pinnacle of motorsport with more driver playlists, exclusive DJ mixes, and a refreshed Formula 1: Sounds of the Circuit playlist that captures the energy of race weekend and beyond.

Immersive Grand Prix details return to Apple Maps in Vegas, enabling F1 fans to explore the race with a comprehensive circuit map showing turn numbers, the finish line, and race cars. Updates include realistic pavement coloring for the track, a refreshed 3D F1 pit building, and more colorful grandstands.

For fans attending in person, Maps makes it easy to get around the race, with useful information about entry gates, rideshare locations, water stations and other amenities, pedestrian walkways and overpasses, road closures, walking directions, and more. In collaboration with the Las Vegas Grand Prix organization, the F1® Heineken Las Vegas Race Week Spots Hyperlocal Guide will showcase places to visit near the circuit, along with fan zones, driver activations, and track features to help build excitement among race-week visitors.

Apple Maps allows fans to explore the race in greater detail, with a comprehensive circuit map showing turn numbers, the finish line, and race cars.

Fans can stay up to date on race weekend in Apple News with notifications and personalized coverage from leading publishers, and can track their favorite drivers and teams for live results, standings, and highlights. Users can also view the race directly within the News app through a special Las Vegas Grand Prix feature and easily jump to the Apple TV app for the full F1 streaming experience.

F1 on Apple TV is available in the U.S. on the Apple TV app on iPhone; iPad; Apple TV 4K; Apple Vision Pro; Mac; popular smart TVs from Samsung, LG, Sony, VIZIO, TCL, and others; Roku and Amazon Fire TV devices; Chromecast with Google TV; and PlayStation and Xbox gaming consoles; and at tv.apple.com, for $14.99 per month with a seven-day free trial for new subscribers. For a limited time, eligible customers who purchase and activate a new iPhone, iPad, Apple TV, or Mac can enjoy three months of Apple TV for free. Visit apple.com/tvpr and see the full list of supported devices.

items.title: Apple Podcasts names Baby, this is Keke Palmer the 2026 Show of the Year
items.summary: Apple Podcasts names Baby, this is Keke Palmer as its 2026 Show of the Year, honoring the podcast for its exceptional quality and cultural impact.
items.body:
Keke Palmer is the host of Baby, this is Keke Palmer, Apple Podcasts’ 2026 Show of the Year.

Today, Apple Podcasts named Baby, this is Keke Palmer its Show of the Year, honoring the podcast for its exceptional quality and cultural impact. Hosted by award-winning multi-hyphenate entertainer Keke Palmer and produced by Wondery and executive produced by Palmer, the show pairs her quick wit with genuine curiosity, striking a balance between humor and thoughtful inquiry that makes even the most recognizable guests feel like close friends. Her natural ability to connect with people draws audiences into every conversation, while her candor and energy bring a refreshing and unique authenticity to the interview format.

Palmer invites some of the biggest names in entertainment and culture to share the experiences that have shaped them. From exploring self-worth with Oprah Winfrey to discussing creativity, reinvention, and fatherhood with Anderson .Paak, she moves effortlessly between laugh-out-loud exchanges and thoughtful reflections on life, relationships, and success. Baby, this is Keke Palmer consistently ranks among the top video and top comedy shows on Apple Podcasts.

Baby, this is Keke Palmer, produced by Wondery and executive produced by Palmer, brings the multi-hyphenate entertainer’s quick wit and genuine curiosity to interviews with today’s biggest voices in culture.

“I’m so honored that Baby, this is Keke Palmer has been named Apple Podcasts’ Show of the Year,” said Palmer. “I love how a conversation about entertainment can open up a bigger conversation about life. There’s so much to explore in the things we watch, laugh at, and connect with, and this show gives me room to follow that curiosity. Thank you to Apple Podcasts, Wondery, our incredible guests, and everyone who listens and brings their own perspective to the conversation. This recognition means so much to me.”

“Keke’s curiosity, humor, and openness make every conversation feel personal, and video brings that connection even closer,” said Oliver Schusser, Apple’s vice president of Podcasts, Music, Sports, and Beats. “Her exceptional craft and cultural impact make Baby, this is Keke Palmer Apple Podcasts’ Show of the Year. We’re proud to celebrate her talent across Apple Podcasts and Apple Music, from the conversations she creates to the music she shares.”

For Palmer, podcasting starts with connection. In an interview with Apple Podcasts for Creators, excerpted below, the host of Baby, this is Keke Palmer shares why she creates room for honest conversation, trusts her curiosity and authenticity, and celebrates being named the Apple Podcasts 2026 Show of the Year.

On creating space for connection: “I’ve spent so much of my life being seen, but being seen and being known are two very different things. … I love that I get to create a space where people can just be people, myself included.”

On following her curiosity: “Preparation is supposed to support the conversation, not control it. I’m always listening for that moment when somebody says something that opens up an entirely new question.”

On bringing authenticity to video: “Don’t try to manufacture a personality for the camera. Develop a relationship with yourself, get comfortable expressing what is already there, and let the camera capture that.”

On being named the Apple Podcasts Show of the Year: “What makes me most proud is that something rooted in genuine curiosity and connection has resonated with other people. It reminds me that being yourself isn’t just personally fulfilling; it can also create value for others. And that’s always been the goal for me.”
